title: The ordinary ringed localization square at an arbitrary sheaf
statement: Let $(C,J),(D,K)$ be small sites, $R_X,R_Y$ commutative coefficient-ring sheaves, $f:(\operatorname{Sh}(J),R_X)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(K),R_Y)$ a ringed-topos morphism [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism], and $A$ any sheaf of sets on $(D,K)$. There exists ordinary comparison data [def-sbc-ringed-sheaf-slice-ordinary-data]: the ringed slice morphism at $A$, the normalized geometric restriction square, mutually mate isomorphisms $f_A^*r_Y\cong r_Xf^*$ and $r_Yf_*\cong f_{A*}r_X$, exact additive restriction functors, preservation of K-injectives by source restriction, and preservation of K-flat complexes with flat terms by target restriction. No derived-category choices, boundedness hypotheses or flatness of the structural map are assumed.

proof.text: Obtain the normalized ordinary ringed and module square from [lem-sbc-ringed-sheaf-slice-ordinary-square]. It supplies the fibre normalizations, structural ring map, the two module adjunctions, and the mutually mate module isomorphisms.

The canonical element restriction is additive and exact, and preserves K-injectives by the proved presentationElementRestriction API in [def-weil-pbc-ringed-presentation-comparison-data]. These results apply to the actual canonical restriction, independently of choices of slice presentation.

The element projection is continuous and cocontinuous by [lem-weil-pbc-element-site-descent]. Its induced ringed restriction has canonical module restriction as left adjoint by [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-cocontinuous-ringed-restriction]. Compare this left adjoint with the tensor pullback supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-supplied-ringed-topos-kflat-pullback] using uniqueness of left adjoints. The latter preserves K-flat complexes with flat terms. Transfer K-flatness across the induced complex isomorphism by tensoring with each acyclic complex; transfer flatness across the termwise isomorphism using the induced isomorphism of tensor functors. This fills the targetKFlat field and proves the entire ordinary comparison theorem.
